prompt: What decides whether an exception class is checked?
hint: Follow `getSuperclass()` upwards.

choices.text: A `checked` flag the class declares in its header
choices.why: There is no such flag; nothing in the class's own header says it.

choices.text: Its ancestors
choices.why: Right: under `RuntimeException` or `Error` it is unchecked, and anywhere else under `Throwable` it is checked.

choices.text: Whether its name ends in `Exception` or in `Error`
choices.why: The suffix is a convention for readers; `NumberFormatException` ends in `Exception` and is unchecked.

choices.text: Whether the JDK or your own program defines it
choices.why: `IOException` is the JDK's and checked; `CatalogueUnavailableException` is yours and unchecked.

prompt: Match each class to the branch `Ancestry` printed for it.
hint: Three lines of output, three branches.

prompt: `Deep` wrapped its recursion in `try { ... } catch (Exception e)`. Why did `after the try` never print?
hint: What does `StackOverflowError` descend from?

choices.text: The `catch` ran, but printing needs stack space that was already gone
choices.why: If the `catch` had matched, `caught an Exception` would have printed first; `grep` counted nothing of the kind.

choices.text: `StackOverflowError` is an `Error`, so `catch (Exception e)` did not match it
choices.why: Right: it never meets `Exception` on its way to `Throwable`.

choices.text: Errors cannot be caught by any `catch` clause
choices.why: `catch (Throwable t)` would have caught it; the section says why that is a bad idea, not an impossible one.

prompt: `Deep`'s output had 1025 lines: one header line and the frames. At how many frames does the JVM stop printing a stack trace?
hint: Subtract the header.

prompt: A colleague writes `catch (Throwable t) { log(t); }` around a whole request handler, so that "nothing can ever crash the server". What is wrong with it?
hint: What does an `Error` say about the JVM?

choices.text: It does not compile, because `Throwable` is abstract
choices.why: `Throwable` is a concrete class, and catching it compiles.

choices.text: Nothing: catching the widest type is the safest choice, since no failure can escape it
choices.why: It is the widest and so the least safe: it also swallows the failures the JVM uses to say it is in trouble.

choices.text: It also catches `Error`s and keeps running on a JVM in trouble
choices.why: Right: after an `OutOfMemoryError` the recovery code itself may not run correctly.

prompt: `LoanNotAllowedException` extends `Exception`. What does that choice make it?
hint: It does not pass through `RuntimeException`.

choices.text: Checked
choices.why: Right: every caller of `lend` must catch it or declare it.

choices.text: Unchecked, because it is a class of your own
choices.why: Who wrote the class does not matter; its ancestors do.

choices.text: An `Error`, because a refused loan stops the program
choices.why: The program carried on and refused politely; nothing about it is an `Error`.

prompt: Why does `LoanNotAllowedException` keep `memberId` as a field when the message already contains it?
hint: Look at what the `catch` in `Desk.main` did with each.

choices.text: The message is lost when the exception is caught
choices.why: `getMessage()` returned it inside the `catch`; nothing was lost.

choices.text: Java requires every custom exception to declare at least one field of its own
choices.why: There is no such rule; `CatalogueUnavailableException` has no field.

choices.text: So a caller uses it as data, not as text
choices.why: Right: `e.memberId()` went to the next step, and the message went to the log.

prompt: `javac Careless.java` failed with `unreported exception LoanNotAllowedException`. Which change fixes it?
hint: Read the rest of the error message.

choices.text: Making `lend` `static`
choices.why: Static or not, `lend` still declares the exception, and the caller still has to deal with it.

choices.text: Catching it in `main`, or adding `throws LoanNotAllowedException` to `main`
choices.why: Right: "must be caught or declared to be thrown" names both ways.

choices.text: Importing `LoanNotAllowedException` at the top of `Careless.java`
choices.why: Both classes are in the same directory and package; the compiler found it, as the message shows.

choices.text: Compiling `Desk.java` and `Careless.java` together, in a single `javac` command, so it sees both
choices.why: The order of compilation changes nothing about what the caller has to do.

prompt: Why is `CatalogueUnavailableException` unchecked while `LoanNotAllowedException` is checked?
hint: Ask what the immediate caller can do about each.

choices.text: Unchecked exceptions are faster to throw
choices.why: Checked or not is a compile-time matter; both are thrown the same way at run time.

choices.text: A cause can only be attached to a `RuntimeException`, never to a checked `Exception`
choices.why: Every `Exception` constructor family has a form with a cause, checked ones included.

choices.text: A caller can tell a member a loan was refused; it cannot fix an unreadable file
choices.why: Right: forcing every caller to catch what it cannot handle only breeds empty `catch` blocks.

prompt: In a stack trace, the original exception passed to the constructor of the new one appears after the words `___ by:`.
hint: `getCause()` returns it.

prompt: The catalogue trace ended with `... 1 more`. What does that line mean?
hint: Compare the last frames of the two parts.

choices.text: The cause shares one frame with the trace above
choices.why: Right: the cause's trace continues into frames the outer trace already printed.

choices.text: There is one more cause, which the JVM did not print
choices.why: A further cause would print as another `Caused by:` section.

choices.text: One frame hit the 1024 limit
choices.why: The limit is about 1024 frames; this trace had about fifteen.

choices.text: The exception was thrown once more after being caught
choices.why: It was thrown once, by `load`, and nothing caught it after that.

prompt: Put the steps of `Catalogue.load` on a missing file in order.
hint: From the JDK's failure to the line printed at the top.
items: the JVM prints the outer exception, then `Caused by:` and the original

prompt: `Fines` printed `fines owed, in cents: 350`. What went wrong?
hint: Look at the `catch` block.

choices.text: `Integer.parseInt` rounded `1O0` down to zero
choices.why: `parseInt` rounds nothing; it threw `NumberFormatException`.

choices.text: An empty `catch` swallowed the failure on line 2 and the loop carried on
choices.why: Right: a failure with a name and a message became a wrong total.

choices.text: The program crashed and printed a partial total
choices.why: It did not crash; that is the problem.

prompt: What does `FinesLoud`'s message add that `NumberFormatException` alone did not have?
hint: What did `parseInt` know, and what did the loop know?

choices.text: The bad value, `1O0`
choices.why: `For input string: "1O0"` already named it; the cause still shows it.

choices.text: Which ledger line, and what it should hold
choices.why: Right: only the loop knew it was line 2 and a number of cents.

choices.text: The stack frames inside `Integer.parseInt`
choices.why: Those came from the cause, which `FinesLoud` kept but did not add.

choices.text: A total of the lines that did parse, so the other members' fines are not lost
choices.why: It printed no total at all, on purpose: no total is better than a wrong one.

prompt: A `catch` block reads `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(e.getMessage()); }`. What does it lose?
hint: Which constructor did it call?

choices.text: Nothing: the message is carried over word for word
choices.why: The words survive; the original's type and stack trace do not.

choices.text: The original exception and its stack trace
choices.why: Right: without the cause there is no `Caused by:`, so where the I/O failed is gone.

choices.text: The checked status, which makes the code refuse to compile
choices.why: Turning a checked exception into an unchecked one compiles; it is a legitimate choice when no caller can handle it.

prompt: What is wrong with `Flow`, which leaves its loop by catching `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`? Choose all that apply.
hint: It printed the right total.

choices.text: The loop has no condition, so a reader must find the `catch` to see where it ends
choices.why: Yes: the intent is hidden in a handler.

choices.text: A real indexing bug would be caught by the same `catch` and print a wrong total
choices.why: Yes: the handler cannot tell the expected end from a mistake.

choices.text: It prints the wrong total
choices.why: It printed 425, which is right; the trouble is what it would do after the next change.

choices.text: The compiler refuses a `for` loop without a condition
choices.why: `for (int i = 0; ; i++)` compiles; an empty condition means true.

prompt: When is an empty `catch` block acceptable?
hint: The section says what the block must contain.

choices.text: When the exception is unchecked
choices.why: `Fines` swallowed an unchecked exception and produced a wrong total.

choices.text: When the exception is "not fatal"
choices.why: "Not fatal" is not a reason on its own; the section asks what would go wrong and why that is acceptable.

choices.text: When a comment in it says why ignoring it is right
choices.why: Right: the next reader can then disagree with a reason instead of guessing at a silence.

prompt: You write `BookNotFoundException` for a lookup by ISBN that finds nothing, and the caller can offer to reserve the book instead. How should it be declared?
hint: Can the caller do something sensible with it?

choices.text: `extends Error`, because a missing book is serious
choices.why: An `Error` is the JVM reporting trouble with itself, not a missing record.

choices.text: `extends Exception`, with the ISBN kept as a field
choices.why: Right: checked, because the caller has a sensible next step, and the ISBN as data for it.

choices.text: `extends Throwable`, so that neither `catch (Exception e)` nor `catch (Error e)` can swallow it
choices.why: Extending `Throwable` directly fits neither branch and surprises every reader; it is not done.

prompt: Lesson 37's suppressed exception and this lesson's cause both put two exceptions in one trace. What is the difference?
hint: Beside, or underneath?

choices.text: A cause is printed first, and a suppressed exception last
choices.why: Both are printed after the main trace; the order is not the difference.

choices.text: Suppressed is for checked exceptions; cause is for unchecked
choices.why: Either kind can be a cause or be suppressed.

choices.text: A suppressed one happened beside it; a cause is why it was thrown
choices.why: Right: a failed close beside a failed use, against a missing file under an unavailable catalogue.

prompt: `Desk.LIMIT` is 2 and `main` tries to lend three books to `ana`. How many `lent` lines does it print?
hint: The third attempt is refused.
